Order
The petitioners are the accused 1 and 2 in CC No.274/2024 on the file of the Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kasargod (Trial Court), which has originated from Crime No.255/2024 registered by the Kasargod Police Station, alleging the commission of the offences punishable under Sections 417, 418, 420 and 406 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. The petitioners state that, by Annexure A2 order, they were granted an order of pre-arrest bail.

However, the learned Sessions Judge, by condition No.3 in the said order, has directed the petitioners to pay Rs.2.5/- lakh to the defacto complainant on or before 25.01.2025, but the payment would not exonerate the petitioners from facing trial for the alleged offence.

Subsequently,
the Investigating Officer filed the charge sheet before the Trial Court, and the case is numbered as CC No.274/2024.

When the case was called on 18.09.2025, CRL.MC NO. 10999 OF 2025 2025:KER:93792 the Trial Court, on finding that the amount of Rs.2.5/- lakh was not paid to CW1 as per the condition in Annexure A2 order, cancelled Annexure A2 order and has issued non-bailable warrants against the petitioners.

The condition in Annexure A2 order, directing the petitioners to deposit Rs.2.5/- lakh, is onerous and Annexure A3 proceedings cancelling the bail and issuing non-bailable warrants against the petitioners are unsustainable in law.
Hence, the Criminal Miscellaneous Case.
3. I have heard the learned Counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor.

4. In Guddan @ Roop Narayan v. State of Rajasthan (2023 LiveLaw (SC) 45), the Honourable Supreme Court, after relying on a plethora of judgments, has held that imposing excessive conditions while granting bail is onerous and tantamounts to refusal of grant of bail.

5. In the case at hand, the Court of Session had granted the petitioners an order of pre-arrest bail,
and directed them to execute a bond for Rs.25,000/-, appear before the Investigating Officer and co-operate with the investigation.

However, the Court of Session has further ordered, by CRL.MC V. Dinesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87315723/
2 NO. 10999 OF 2025 2025:KER:93792 condition No.3, the petitioners to pay Rs.2.5/- lakh to the defacto complainant, with a rider that it would not exonerate them from facing the trial.

sentences.text: 6. The above condition, according to me, is onerous and unsustainable in law and is against the settled principles of law laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court and this Court in a catena of decisions that bail Court shall not impose impossible and onerous bail conditions, rendering the bail order nugatory and redundant.

7. It is only in view of the above impugned and unsustainable condition that the Trial Court, on finding that the petitioners have failed to pay the amount to the defacto complainant, has suo-motu cancelled the bail, which again is erroneous and beyond the jurisdiction of the Trial Court, and that too without affording the petitioners an opportunity of being heard.
On an overall consideration of the facts and the reasons stated above, I am satisfied that this is a fit case to exercise the inherent powers of this Court under Section 528 of the BNSS.

Accordingly, I allow the Criminal Miscellaneous CRL.MC NO. 10999 OF 2025 2025:KER:93792 Case by setting aside condition No.3 in Annexure A2 order and further setting aside Annexure A3 proceedings dated 18.09.2025, cancelling the bail granted to the petitioners and issuing non-bailable warrants against them.
The petitioners are permitted to participate in the case on the basis of the bail bonds executed by them pursuant to Annexure A2 order, which stands modified by this order.
